title: Small expressions, precise answers
description: Synthetic demonstration authored for QuizReceipt. Three JavaScript expressions show exact option labels, individual explanations and a downloadable feedback record. Choose an answer for each question, or leave one unanswered to see that state.

questions.prompt:
What does this expression return?

Object.is(NaN, NaN)

options.label: true
options.explanation: Object.is considers NaN the same value as NaN.

options.label: false
options.explanation: NaN === NaN is false, but Object.is uses different equality semantics.

options.label: Throws a TypeError
options.explanation: Both arguments are valid JavaScript values. This call completes normally.

questions.explanation: Object.is compares values using the SameValue algorithm. Its treatment of NaN differs from strict equality.

questions.prompt:
What does this expression return?

typeof null

options.label: "null"
options.explanation: The typeof operator has no null result string.

options.label: "object"
options.explanation: JavaScript reports null as object through typeof, a historical behavior of the language.

options.label: "undefined"
options.explanation: typeof undefined returns this string. Null and undefined are different values.

questions.explanation: The result is the string object. Use value === null when you specifically need to detect null.
